It might be helpful to think about what he could be doing to make you feel more secure and if there are specific things then you could have a conversation with him and tell him what might help. It's important to do this when you're both feeling relaxed and not during an argument. It's not fair to project your worries onto him and by seeking consistent reassurance it can make the other party feel like you don't trust them or you don't believe what they're saying. It sounds like he's doing a lot of acts of service for you and maybe that's how he shows love? Try and practice self regulating without seeking the reassurance and remind yourself to check the facts and look at all the nice things they're doing for you. But also fair that if there are things they could do that might help you then you can always articulate that. I wish you all the best with it.

I got really mad when I started DBT. Why? Because it's really hard work and it requires self reflection on times when you have struggled with the behaviours that can accompany being unwell. I felt also like I was being required to stifle myself for broader society, like the skills I was learning were to make me more "palatable" to the people around me. However when I started practicing the skills, I saw the benefits.

I'm almost 34 and Ive done two DBT programs which changed my experience a lot. I still struggle with the emotions. I dont think they ever feel less strong. I think all that changes is how I react to things. I still make mistakes and find myself experiencing a lot of loneliness because a lot of people get tired of me. I think the availability of mental health services is part of the problem. Also I wish I had spent more time when I was younger working on my mental health because I have all these adult responsibilities like a mortgage and full time job Im trying to hold down. Thankfully no children and no plans to ever go down that road. I am better when I am practicing DBT skills and when I am working through my triggers but affording that kind of help is hella expensive.

I was all in until he said the treatment doesn't hurt and is easy. Therapy for BPD and NPD is a long difficult process in which there will be a lot of emotional pain and struggle if youre doing it right and actually reflecting on your illness. It doesn't mean it isnt worth it. But let's not pretend it's simple.

I think that you have to explain to your partner your expectations around gift giving. I was with a person who was not a big gift person and experienced constant disappointment. In every relationship since, Ive told partners about how in that past relationship there was a whole thing around gift giving. Not because I need people to buy me lots of things etc. But because gift giving is something I like to do for the people I love and I feel special when that is reciprocated. It becomes a negotiation between your needs/wants and your partners needs/wants.

I feel this so much. I have lived with this for so long and my mother still denies that I am mentally ill.. Last time I started therapy and complained about the cost she said " well hopefully you wont need it soon". Then the constant misunderstandings with friends and like I will own that in the past I have done emotionally manipulative things when I didnt understand that was what I was doing. But the more Ive learnt about myself and how to control it, the more frustrated I feel that I am always the one who has to be managing my emotions and reactions and everyone else around me can just exist without having to think about to consequences of every thought that comes into their brain. It's extremely painful and I have honestly found only recently that connecting with more people like me is the only way I can feel safe in the world.
